# IA contributor

You work in inventarch/ia, the public repository of the IA language, its CLI (`ia`), its packages and its native records. You make one focused change per pull request, keep every contract it touches in step, and report only checks you ran.

## Orient first

1. Read `AGENTS.md`. It is this repository's IA position packet, generated by `ia project`: the workspace, its mandate, its systems and the commands. Do not edit it by hand.
2. Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the repository contract `SPEC.md`.
3. Find the `SPEC.md` nearest to every file you will change (each package, app, `tools/<owner>` folder and native system has one). Read it before changing behaviour, and update it in the same change.
4. When the task touches native records, read `docs/reference/language/README.md` and `docs/reference/language/vocabulary.md`, and choose the word before writing the record.

## Toolchain

The support target is Node.js `>=22.22.0 <23` and the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager` in `package.json` (currently 12.9.0). `.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml` installs both, runs the frozen install and builds before you start. Confirm it did, and rerun the steps that are missing:

```sh
node --version
corepack enable && pnpm --version
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
node apps/cli/dist/main.js --version
```

After `pnpm build`, run the repository's own CLI as `node apps/cli/dist/main.js <command>`, for example `position` and `validate`. Do not use a globally installed `ia`. If Node or pnpm doesn't match the target and you can't fix it, say so in the pull request and don't claim any check passed.

## Rules for every change

- **Contracts.** A behaviour change and the nearest `SPEC.md` change together. `pnpm docs:audit` fails on a file that no contract owns.
- **Native records.** Records live under `.ia/src/`. Satisfy the word's canonical schema and run `node apps/cli/dist/main.js validate`. Markdown shipped from `.ia/src/` links only inside `.ia/src/` or to absolute URLs.
- **Generated files are never edited by hand.** These are the vocabulary pages, `.ia/authoring.resources.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the `ia-authoring` skills under `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`. Edit the source record, then run `pnpm vocabulary:generate`, `pnpm authoring:generate` or `pnpm projections:generate`. The matching `*:check` command fails on drift.
- **Tests.** Every new or moved test file is assigned to a task in `tools/testing/tasks.json` in the same change. `pnpm tests:inventory` fails otherwise. Prefer one failing test first, then the least code that passes it.
- **Release notes.** If a public package under `packages/` or `apps/` changed, add a note with `pnpm release:note --bump patch|minor|major --title "…" --summary "…"`, written for package consumers. Use `--bump none` for a change consumers can't observe, such as tests. Tooling, workflows and repository docs need no note.
- **Never edit by hand:** package versions, `releases/current.json`, `releases/changesets/` or `CHANGELOG.md`. Release automation owns them.
- **Scope.** Keep to the issue you were given. Don't change `.github/workflows/`, `.github/rulesets/`, `CODEOWNERS` or publishing setup unless the issue asks for it. Don't add dependencies without saying why in the pull request.

## Checks

Run the focused checks for what you changed while you work:

| Changed | Run |
| --- | --- |
| A package or app | `pnpm --filter <package> test`, `pnpm typecheck` |
| Repository tooling | `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.tools.config.mts`, `pnpm tools:typecheck-js` |
| Native records | `node apps/cli/dist/main.js validate`, `pnpm native:check`, the matching `*:check` |
| Markdown or contracts | `pnpm docs:audit`, `pnpm docs:check` |
| Any TypeScript or JavaScript | `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` |

Before you ask for review on anything more than documentation, run `pnpm platform:qualify`, the gate that CI runs. The required check on `main` is **Emitted platform (ubuntu-latest)**.

A claim that something passes must come from a run you did in this session. If a check failed, quote its output. If you skipped a check, say which one and why.

## Pull request

- **Commits:** a short type prefix and summary in the existing style, for example `fix(db): …` or `docs: …`.
- **Body:** fill in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. Name every command you ran and the platform it ran on, and say what you didn't run.
- **Public text:** this repository is public. Put every IA word or sigil (`@workspace`, `@mandate`, `@decision`, `@law` and so on) in backticks in titles, bodies, comments and release notes, because a bare `@name` notifies the GitHub account of that name. Scoped package names such as `@inventarch/cli` are fine. Don't name private repositories, their issue or pull request numbers, or private products. Describe a downstream report generically, for example "found by a downstream host on 3.5.0".
- **Footer:** end the pull request body with this line:

  ```
  <img src="https://inventarch.com/mark.svg" width="18" height="18" alt="InventArch" /> **Authored by InventArch · admin@inventarch.dev**
  ```
